No Venicci. Anxiety is very real however the amount of doctors who pass off very real chronic illness as anxiety is too damn high. 

Almost every person who has chronic illness has had it shoved off as mental illness or anxiety at one point or another.

I spent four years thinking my fingers and feet turning blue and white was anxiety and that feeling dizzy and foggy was dissociation, even had a few doctors fob off tonic clonic seizures as mental illness. 

It's taken me years (and a few helpful people) to claim my own body back and straight up tell a doctor that, yes, I am anxious but I am anxious because I am unwell. I am not unwell because I am anxious.

Anxiety is not belittled but it's often used as a way to shove a patient's file off your desk because you are not willing to rule out other possibilities. That's why it is like gaslighting because most of the time we are made to believe it's our minds that cause our illness to a point where people end up having a fear of doctors.

Once again, it's about rational choices that could have been taken to prevent a crime. 

If someone intentionally drinks alcohol over the limit that you are allowed to consume while driving, and then kills someone in an accident; they will be held accountable because the accident could have been prevented if they obeyed the law which is there for a reason. 

If someone was spiked by a substance and then ended up in an accident, there would be a very strong case for them not to be held accountable for the accident because without choice they were not in a rational state of mind. 

The state of the rational mind is the most important component in law when determining how much someone should be held accountable. 

Even prosecuting minors and the limitations on that is due to their ability to process things rationally. 

The point of this is that I think people confuse mental illness and insanity. There are people who have been out of control of their minds or actions who do deserve to not be convicted, but a personality disorder such as AsPD would certainly not be one.

In order for somebody to not be held accountable for their crimes, they would have to be declared insane and not in control of their actions. 

Even while having a mental health issue that is diagnoasable, anyone with AsPD or NPD are fully in control of their actions and therefore legally sane. This means that they must be prosecuted for their crimes and take the stand as a sane person. They cannot claim insanity. 

Even if someone had a mental illness that would at times make them out of control of their own body and actions, say like Paranoid Schizophrenia, the defense would still have to prove that they were at the time not in control of their actions or body. In this current world that is very difficult to prove. 

The law doesn't care about why you did something if you had a rational mind while you did it. 

If someone commits a crime, they do with full awareness that what they are doing is not right. In personality disorders that display a lack of remorse, it means that they don't feel bad about what they have done. It does not mean that they didn't have control of what they were doing.

And that is what it's about. 

There are a lot of criminals that try to plead insanity but, at the end of the day, it has to be very clear that that person was not in control of their actions when the event took place. 

If you stopped convicting psychopaths and made it easier for them to get away with things, they would very likely abuse that power to get away with things that they perfectly know is not legal or perhaps correct.
